Its hard for me to give this game a negative review. If there were a middle option, I’d give it something like a 5/10.

The game has very nice visuals, music, and the overall feel is genuinely pleasant. However, it suffers from a few issues that make me write a negative review. The first is balance and variety. There aren’t many options for experimenting, and once you figure out which build is the strongest, playing anything else doesn’t make sense. There’s no enjoyment in testing something different because it simply doesn’t work, (the bomb is overpowered). Next, some enemies can softlock you if you don’t have the right build for them. For example, blocking a specific tile completely ruins the fun when you’re only playing around three of them. Another aspect is the grind and the length of the game. With the right build, completing the game 100% took me about 2.5 hours, which is a bit disappointing considering how many possibilities could have been added to make it more varied.

I get the impression it’s like a teaser for a bigger roguelike, there’s very little content. But for that price, I can live with it.

To sum up, the game is really enjoyable and I had a good 2.5 hours with it, but there’s no point coming back to it after one win, so a big downside for replayability (not to be confused with grind because grind is not replayability)

Disappointingly short and a bit repetitive gameplay wise.

Aesthetics and polish are amazing but the synergies are very limited and the game stops you from upgrading your build after a certain point which is not very fun.

Really wish there was a "middle" rating. The game is worth checking out, you'll be done in a few hours and there's not a ton to go back to once you're done.

The core gameplay is pseudorandom with some really neat "skill" mechanics.
Beats are chill.
Clicking is fun. Wheels are fun. Gambling is fun.

There's very little replayability as of now (will be interesting to see what comes in future updates).
There's one pretty OP path to completing the game and some other paths only really materialize if you have unlocked points in other things.
Enemies and strategy being linear, it makes it hard to recommend. But if you go in with "can I get 6-7 bucks of entertainment in 4 hours" -- yeah, you sure can.

hope the dev expands on the idea (even in a sequel).

I really wanted to like Slots & Daggers, but it feels too short and shallow. The slot machine roguelike concept is cool, but there is not enough variety to keep things interesting. Compared to Balatro, which builds tons of depth from a simple idea through strong synergies and run variety, Slots & Daggers feels solved very quickly. Once you get the few key items, most runs play out the same. Nearly every build relies on the same core items that give extra spins, so it becomes more about speeding through fights than making decisions. I finished my first run within my first few hours and unlocked almost everything shortly after. It is not a bad game, but it does not have enough content or replayability for me to recommend it.

It's a neat game, but there just isn't enough of it. 
 
I had the strategy figured out and beat the game in under 3 hours. The rest of the playtime was for the Arena mode, where I beat an enemy that was clearly intended to be impossible and then the game just threw me into the start of the main story rather than give any sort of ending. 
 
Balance is generally messed up. The obviously good options are so obviously good that there's little thought into how you maximise your strategy. And if you figure out the really busted build the game basically plays itself. It's a fun little puzzle to figure out for the first hour or two but there's not enough to justify the price tag.

I think this game is meant as a demo if anything. Dont get me wrong its very fun to see high numbers but I got all the achievments and got all the unlocks within 3 hours. I dont consider myself a particularly good gamer to do that. I just feel like at its current state it doesnt provide much content or replayability. I was hoping something like balatro but it fell very short. I do hope the game succeeds cause its a fun idea but as of now I find it lacking. Also my pc depsite being able to run games like Resident evil 4 on the highest graphics cant even get above 60 fps in this game. So overall the optimization is bad and the replayability sadly not there. I do hope it gets better...

Has some interesting points, but not a very satisfying progress loop. 
few strategies that will get you to the end game. 
mostly about repeating until you getting stat upgrades rather than focusing on strategy.

Was awesome until the dev felt the need to either nerf or develop counters for any build that made the game "easy".  Found a fun build that seemed to be doing well only to find out others complained it made the game easy, so now I just get the punishment for it. There's been like five updates in one week all nerfing or countering something. The only time I'm even hearing of the really good builds is when they're being dealt with.

Immaculate design, great sound. 
It’s just… not fun. At all. There are very little ways to feel you are applying skill to the game, and a brief experimentation of different combos felt dull. I felt no connection to the (nicely drawn) enemies. It could have been faceless bots I was attacking one after the other. During “combat”, there is no way to adjust strategy. Between combats, there are very limited ways. 
Wish this game had worked for me! Just too much rng

Lacks depth in its current state. I was very excited to play the full version. Progress carried over from the demo (which was very fun), but I beat the entire game on my first run. less than one hour. I don't really know what to do at this point. If you didn't play the demo and want 2 hours of fun game play get it. If you are looking for more than that I would steer clear. I am very disappointed that it was as short as it was.
It feels bad that there is no variety and no reason to replay the game.
good concept, but very barebone. after a couple of hours, there's not much else.

I played for 6 hours and… I didn’t like it. 
First of all, the game’s polish is excellent. Visually, it’s so well put together that it’s impossible not to like it; however, if we look at the systems and mechanics, we can see exactly where the game falls flat. To begin with, if you’re giving the player a choice, you need to ensure those choices are meaningful enough, and that’s not the case here. There aren’t enough items. Choosing between items doesn’t offer much in the way of freedom. So, in the end, a solid visual foundation has been laid, but unfortunately, the systems haven’t been developed to match it.

I played the demo for about an hour and had really high expectations for this game, so I bought it right away on release day. I was genuinely hoping for several, maybe even a dozen or more hours of great fun. Unfortunately, I’m disappointed — on my second playthrough I completed all the game’s content, which took me around 70 minutes. The game really had huge potential, but it didn’t live up to my expectations. For now, I’m getting a refund — I’m disappointed.

It's a great game which feels extremely juicy, but the lack of content quickly becomes apparent. The developer isn't addressing this issue, and almost silently quitting on the title.
This is sad, given that the game has all the assets and gears in place, and simply needs more content in the same direction for it to flourish. Hopefully, the developer will realise this with time, and more content will allow me to change my review.

The visuals are nice, but there are few builds, and the game itself is very short; I finished it in literally an hour. I didn't refund, hope the author continues to develop the game. So, the idea and visual - yes. The depth - no.

Really short game, not worth it. Dev promised more, never came back.

Shame, could have been a great game.
Finished it in 2,2 hours. It looks quite nice but the mechanics are too simple, even for the small price.

The gameplay's good, but I (like many others on the forum) unlocked all of the meta progression after a single run, due to what seems to be a bug. I then went on to beat all of the game's content and get 100% achievements in just 79 minutes of play time. No additional difficulty options, nothing. Very poor replayability that was amplified by an unfortunate bug. In addition, the game lacks QoL features: no speed-up, and you need to spin each slot individually, which is five slots per turn. There's no option to spin all slots at once, for example.
If it were just the bug, I wouldn't be leaving this review, but sadly I feel robbed. Which is tough to do with a game that costs €5. But there's nothing left to do!

Too short, not enough skill expression or interaction, not enough content. Once you figure out the best things you can beat the game and once you have enough meta progression you can beat the game with anything else.
The game is really bare bones. It has a great look and feel but the actual gameplay its not there. There are no fun combos, no different builds, no eureka moments and no new mechanics to learn.

All right, so every other opinion is either written by bots or uses AI because they are so stupid. I'm going to be honest here so you can know if you want this game or not: it's a good game for dopamine, but there are four issues with it. And I'm going to talk only about issues.

Firstly, it's genuinely so f^cking short. Maximum four hours if you have an average IQ. Mostly because even after end-game, you have nothing to do anyway since all of the items are unlocked. 

Secondly, half of the items are relatively useless, but once you have a good strategy - mine was inf coins with the gambling gem and money % amplifier - you can pretty much win the whole game, even with zero personal upgrades from the tokens. 

Thirdly, the game is unbalanced as hell, which is kind of bad for an rpg. So many items don't make sense because they're so bad[Which is pretty serious when the game has like, what, 30 items max?], and you'll pretty much be forced to do skill shots with physical weapons and amplifiers throughout the entire game. Essentially, every run is the same. Nothing differs at all. 
It goes like this:
1 - You pick a heavy sword, a coin and a shield as a starting kit, cuz everything else is trash, like I said before.
2 - You upgrade the heavy sword and make your own kit [like a large shield and a coin bag, for example].
3 - You again just upgrade everything while buying and upgradeing random artefacts that you like. You will most likely get the Dracula artefact which has lifesteal,

You know those people sitting in the casino that just pull the lever over and over and look bored and dead inside as they lose over and over? Now with the joys of modern game development, that can be you.

[h1]Fun for a little over an hour, but honestly gets boring after that.[/h1]

The art is beautiful, and the objects moving around the table look amazing. However, the gameplay itself feels [b]flat and shallow[/b]. I get that it's called 'Slots', but it really needs a higher [b]skill factor[/b]. It doesn't make sense to lose a great run just because luck decided not to give me a shield; there should be a skill-based alternative. Some weapons already have skill checks, so I think this concept should be applied to defense as well.

[b]Ironically[/b], the game also feels broken in the opposite way. If I start in a later [b]level[/b], I get so much starting cash that I can just create whatever build I want immediately. You basically defeated the purpose of the 'Slots' name since I can just use the starting money to bypass the mechanics.

I figured everything out in an hour. [b]The game is not bad, but definitely not good.[/b]

It's not for me. I expected this game to be silly, casual fun. But even for this type of game, I just find it too shallow, and too passive. You're literally mostly just clicking and waiting for an enemy health bar to tick down. It's basically an auto battler, except it requires an absurd amount of clicking. I also find it strange that such a simple game doesn't have controller support. I guess it technically works, but it's super clunky. Alternating between advancing turns and using items proves especially tedious. So yeah, I fail to see the appeal, and even at its low price point I can't recommend it.

TL:DR - I want to rate Slots & Daggers neutral. It really is a great game and worth the experience at the price tag. I would say full price is worth it, even more so at a discount.

[b]As of this review, the last update to the game was Nov, 2025. Seems like the dev isn't returning as of right now. [/b]

[b]The Okay[/b]

[b]The Bad[/b]

[b]What I Would Want[/b]

* Balance fixes

People might say that we shouldn't expect updates and I guess that's true except for when its a roguelike. We all buy these games knowing they're repetitive with assets that get used over and over with little to no variety but the game will receive updates for a year minimum.

But balance is simply not there. There are builds (circular saw + gem + hammer/sling) that are just too easy and you discover them as soon as you get basics of the gameplay

I'm sad to give this game a thumbs down. It feels harsh, considering I only paid €5. The UI has all the bells and whistles to make every hit incredibly satisfying. But that's about it - and everything else feels like wasted potential. I finished the game in just over four hours, taking out all the enemies in one shot on my last run. I feel like I've already seen all the content. The game is unbalanced, with some weapons clearly overpowered and others distinctly disappointing. I would have liked to see this game developed for at least another six months, and I'd happily pay double the current price for it to reach its full potential.

The progression is really cockeyed; you can select for your starting equipment a very powerful piece of melee weaponry that there's really no reason to ever replace. Also, because it's a slot machine, the fewer symbols you have the better your odds of seeing any one of them - and therefore, the better the odds of getting 3-in-a-row for a "critical hit". In practice, you settle on a set of three reels that you like, and keep them for the rest of the game. 
 
Also, this doesn't feel like a slot machine. Getting 3 in a row gives you a crit, but 4 in a row isn't a thing. Each individual symbol fires off when it's shown, which makes it feel more like a dice game that gives you bonuses for triples. 
 
Combat balancing is peak frustration, with enemies that can one-shot you from full health with an armor-piercing attack for a round-one instakill. Not my favorite experience. 
 
In short, this doesn't work for me as a slot machine game, and it doesn't work for me as an RPG.
feels like an early access game. Fun for exactly 3 hours then u get through the entire game.

Great potential for an addictive rogue-like but fell short. It took me about 4 hours to finish the game, there were not many viable builds since the reroll mechanic is so OP. The money caps out at $100. The opponents increase in being bigger dmg sponges and more damage, with only a few with interesting attacks that could make gameplay interesting. 

I hope the dev continues to add more to the game, the ceiling is a bit low at the moment with the latter 1/3 of the game being extremely repetitive once you've completed your build. It's a well executed but shallow game right now and may not be worth the price, but I love supporting solo projects! ymmv, but maybe this will encourage the dev to consider how they can scale the game. 

Potetial bug: the power up shop doesn't have new stock past a certain point, even if you sell one to make room, you lose it forever and the shop remains empty.

I wish there was a middling option but as it is I'll have to give this game a thumbs down unfortunately.

There's a lot to like here in terms of game "juice" - i.e. the animations, effects, sound effects, music, flashing lights etc but this feels like the best part of the game. The enemy design is quite samey in terms of how they feel to fight, and while the pixel art for each enemy is cool its so small you don't get a great feel for it.

The game has loads of items but ones that "skill check" you on roll make the run tedious as sometimes you'll have to do 5 skill checks in a row, or just whiff them if it doesn't particularly matter. Although I do like how you can time the big sword to deliberately do 0 damage to farm gold. But the most powerful items don't require skill checks and after a fair few failed runs you'll realise which items you need to get further to the end - unless I was doing something wrong a lot of the items just have no hope of scaling enough to even register as damage on the late game enemies. From what I can tell there are a couple of viable late game builds but all of them revolve around the same concept with just your damage dealing item swapped out.

One issue is that about halfway through the run on a viable run you'll have all your core items maxed out in terms of levels so when the ingame shop pops up after each enemy, you'll have nothing to buy. Looks fun at first with nice art, but the gameplay is basically non-existent, okay for an hour or two but that's about it. Maybe later with a little more content it could be a fun campaign

There are some good aspects in this game and could be a good potential, but the game in total look like a rather demo than full game. I finished one run and there is nothing else to do. Lack of strategy and soon getting boring.
Very well put together... just a horrible base game design. The idea sounds neat but when executed in this way you have very little control as the player.

Overall, the idea is good, the graphics are amazing, the background sound is nice, and the game is catchy. It took me about 6 hours to reach 12 achievements, after which it suddenly became boring.

However, speaking objectively, I wouldn’t recommend a game where only one build is viable. You have to skip about 90% of the weapons and skills, and the game forces you to play what’s effective rather than what you actually want.

For now, I’d rate it 4/10. Looking forward to future updates and greater build diversity.

I enjoyed the game immensely. However it is a short lived joy. The game can easily be broken with the right combo namely, bombs, diamonds, and another rotary blade. Ultimately making the game feeling hollow and pointless. I cannot fully say you may not enjoy this, but without further content and challenges beyond min/maxing it will be a short, tiresome chore rather than a game. Be wary of these inexpensive indie games, often times they fail to properly plan out their content.

Its a decent game, with cool art but it is way too short, I finished the game after 3 -4 tries.
If you used the bomb with all the repeat items like 2x, sawmill and jewel you would win the entire game by spinning just once for each boss.
If i figured this out 10 mins earlier i would have refunded the game.
A good game if you just wanna pass a couple hrs but nothing more.

The content is way too short. I finished the main story, if there is one, within 2 hours. Didn't even unlock everything yet. Builds are not balanced at all. The price is too high for this much of content, I would give a higher rating if this game is cheaper or free.

finished the game in 2.7 hours... kinda too short

not many strategies involved

I feel bad writing this because I don't like leaving bad reviews for games, but I just was pretty disappointed. I really wanted to like this game. I love goblins, rougelikes, and gambling games, so I thought this would be perfect for me. However, I found this game more frustrating than fun. The game feels almost impossible to get far in without getting the modifiers, which you can only unlock by playing the game more. I don't mind some roguelite elements every once in a while, but the game feels like the only way to really go far in the game is with those roguelite elements. There are some aspects of strategy, but not enough to make your choices in the game feel meaningful, especially when at the end of your run you can just get modifiers that do more than all the thought and strategy you put into the choices you made in the game. So you're left either feeling like the only way to spin the slot machine well is to spin it more, or that you have to be perfect at doing the skill checks (there are only two) and at timing the wheel perfectly. But even if you're perfect at the skill checks, you still are barely able to get far without grinding for those modifiers. Also even if I was primarily relying on skill checks to get far in the game, I felt like I was missing out on the whole "slot machine" theme and just bruteforcing my way through the game. This game feels like a short demo that was extended by a frustrating, grindy progression system instead of adding any meaningful conten

Presentation is great, sound is great, the Idea is generally cool.

It comes with a few major problems:
1.) The gambling through slot machine gameplay doesnt work well, because its not plannable or influential enough.
You can try to line up by pressing stop at the right time, but it still ends up to be too much of a gamble to call it skill.
Because of it not needing skill but being random/luck based, the entire gameplay consists of pressing a button and creating your "build" out of a too narrow selection of items/symbols.

Picking new symbols is rarely a good idea, because why would you add another weapon lvl 1 decreasing your chance to hit your existing lvl 3 weapon?
I asked that myself a lot while playing and came to the conclusion that the game has a design problem OR lacks complexity to provide valuable effects.
Theres also no combos or dependencies, no chain effects or anything going on, supporting the use of symbol combinations.

Some sort of combo sets that you can get would have added a lot of depth.
Like hitting with 3 different types of daggers causes another roll or shield and hammer causes Shield Bash which adds the armor to your damage and stuns.


2.) The main problem through all of that, is the content is not there.
In my less than 2 hours (112 minutes) i unlocked nearly all items (only 3 more to go) and got to the final level (failed it sadly).
That means i am about 20 minutes short to finish the game in its entirety.

very fun game. Played it a bunch around launch and waited for new content. Unfortunately the game doesn't seem to be getting any updates :(

There isn't much to the game beyond pulling a lever and watching flashing lights on a wheel. You have some choices to make between rounds, but usually not enough to substantially affect your run. The roguelite elements of the game and out-of-run upgrades you can get make early losses feel inevitable, and later wins feel trivial. The skill challenge mini games you get for some weapons can be fun, but they get old fast and can't carry a game alone. The enemies are effectively all the same, and even the enemies that are different in ways I could identify, there isn't really any way to approach them differently or change your strategy because by the time you know what you are fighting, all the decisions you could make have already been made, and all there is to do is pull the lever. 
 
Could be I just don't gel with slot machines in the same way I could with other randomness formats like Dice or cards, but this game couldn't grab me the way other similar games did.

The game is truly amazing, the art, sound and even screen shake are truly amazed me. Though, I complete this game on my 7th hours of the game. For me, the game is too short and I don't see any update incoming from the dev. Some upgrades and weapons are to powerful and I keep choosing those upgrade to win this game, after found the best recipe there is no reason to choose another upgrade, this is just not what I expected.

I don't normally write reviews but I feel a bit cheated with this one.  This pains me to write, but I wish I would have known this before buying.  

The game itself is very fun, very well polished.  Its a blast to actually play for a few moments.  But this fun vanishes faster than with any other roguelike i've ever played.  There 3 main problems with it imo.  

1) its incredibly short.  One of the things I like about roguelikes, is the ability to continuously play the game over and over again.  In my book, a roguelike should provide at least 10-20 hours of fun before it loses its thrill.  Slots & Daggers does not give anywhere close to that level of gameplay.  If it wasn't so polished, I'd say it was an early access game.  There just isn't enough content.   Furthermore, even the content that exists isn't dynamic enough.  I found there were basically 1-2 builds that were viable, the rest were a slog to play.  This greatly reduces the replayability.  Basically after my 7th run, I beat the game and felt no need to play again.  Let's just say this, I've never played a roguelite (the kind that lets you upgrade in between runs that make your next run stronger) where you beat the game WELL before finishing the meta upgrade tree.  Well in this game there are about 8ish stat upgrades-- things like increase physical damage 10%, revive after dying, increase gold gained etc... No joke, the game is easily beatable after only getting 2/8 upgrades.  It actually blew my mind.

very beautiful game and cute concept but 90% of items are useless and I'm pretty sure there's only a single viable build

3.9 Hours and have 100%'d the game without much tangible difficulty. 
Might make this review positive if more content for it is on the horizon, it kinda needs it as it's preeeetty empty, even for the price.  
Don't get me wrong, I enjoy this kind of game but it's not often I get this little real playtime out of a paid game.

Is it knowingly stated to be a short game? Yes. Is it a fun game? Also yes. Then why the negative review?

Dev ghosted his project after committing to bug fixes, rebalancing, and content updates. It turned from a "support a solo dev" project to a "cash grab & run" scenario.

It's a great baseline for a game with so much potential, but the balancing is way off right now, with the game boiling down to bigger number = better, with seemingly no room for build types and strategy, because by the 3rd map the enemies either one shot you, or you one shot them.

It is an extremely small and short game with little replayability. For me, its worth 2-3€ but everything above that is a tall ask. I cant recommend it even though its kinda cute and creative. I wish it was better.
The game is interesting, but with the muted dull colors it loses luster, enough that it takes away from the game play, everything just looks the same and the excitement of advancement is lost.

It is not a bad game, it has great music and art style, but the gameplay is basic, kinda clunky and badly balanced. 
 
The enemies scale is such a way that some weapons are worthless and there is just not enough variety nor synergy to make them worthwhile to make a run with them.

there's too little content, it feels unfinished, (content wise). and the balance is waaaaay off, so really, there's only o n e, just oooo nnnneeeeee build that is viable, and that is armor + axe + gold + that one weapon that deals dmg based on gold, the visual polish and game feel is okay, but seriously hurt, to the point all the effort turned 'useless' by the lackluster audio fx. it's 2 hours short, from start to finish, no build variety, replayability, pretty much none, simply because there's nothing to experiment with. it really shouldn't cost 8 euro's, as there's competition that provide so much better value.
very repetitive and short. it doesn't hold up to the excellent roguelites out there. there is no meaningful decision making involved, it feels a lot like those old incremental upgrade flash games.

I recommend this game, with a big caveat, more on that below.
The art direction is wonderful and the game is incredibly stylish. Mechanics are tight and responsive, the game runs beautifully and the music and sound design are great, too. It's easy to get into and even easier to get lost in despite its major flaws which I will get to now.

If you are an avid roguelite enjoyer and love them for their difficulty and replayability. Why?
Well, simply put, it's too easy and there's too little variation between runs. I had feared this when I played the demo, and my fear turned out to be justified. 
It's very easy to piece together a run where you get very consistent damage output, and it only gets worse as you progress into the game. You scale very strongly with the meta upgrades, and the game can't really keep up. This is especially true if you get good at the skillcheck minigames and cobble together a build that spams respins. This is in part due to the low ammount of items/powerups in the game, making not rolling the good ones right away very forgiving. You rarely get into a situation where you have to make do with items you don't like because the ones you want just aren't turning up. As you unlock more stuff, this gets better, but it's vastly offset by the very powerful meta-upgrades in the game.
